Wait, the rule says: "Counter triangle (a BONUS, not an automatic win): spearman counters knight; archer counters spearman; knight counters archer. Having the counter multiplies your force by 1.5."
"The MOST NUMEROUS type of each army sets the counter matchup (ties in count break in the order spearman, archer, knight)."
So attacker's most numerous is spearman. Defender's most numerous is archer.

Archer counters spearman. So the defender (archer) counters the attacker's most numerous (spearman).
So defender's force is multiplied by 1.5!

Attacker's force: 31 spearmen (attack 31) + 8 archers (attack 16) + 6 knights (attack 24) = 71.
Since attacker's most numerous is spearman, and defender's most numerous is archer, the defender has the counter. But does the attacker get any counter? Knight counters archer, but attacker's most numerous is spearman, not knight. So no counter bonus for attacker.
So attacker's effective force is 71.
Defender's effective force is 22.5.
71 > 22.5, so attacker wins easily, despite the counter bonus.

In simultaneous turn-based games, troops that are ordered to move are no longer present in the origin village for defense in the same turn. They are "on the march".
So if I send Madrid's troops to Burgos, Madrid has 0 troops to defend against an attack this turn.

And "Orders are SIMULTANEOUS".
